item.title: Go Daily Question 189
item.description:
If the calling code for the Add() function is:

func main() {
 var a Integer = 1
 var b Integer = 2
 var i interface{} = &a
 sum := i.(*Integer).Add(b)
 fmt.Println(sum)
}

Then the correct definition for the Add function is:

A.
type Integer int
func (a Integer) Add(b Integer) Integer {
 return a + b
}

B.
type Integer int
func (a Integer) Add(b *Integer) Integer {
 return a + *b
}

C.
type Integer int
func (a *Integer) Add(b Integer) Integer {
 return *a + b
}

D.
type Integer int
func (a *Integer) Add(b *Integer) Integer {
 return *a + *b
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

A, C

item.title: Go Daily Question 110
item.description:
If the calling code for the Add() function is:

func main() {
 var a Integer = 1
 var b Integer = 2
 var i interface{} = &a
 sum := i.(*Integer).Add(b)
 fmt.Println(sum)
}

Then the correct definition for the Add function is:

A.
type Integer int
func (a Integer) Add(b Integer) Integer {
 return a + b
}

B.
type Integer int
func (a Integer) Add(b *Integer) Integer {
 return a + *b
}

C.
type Integer int
func (a *Integer) Add(b Integer) Integer {
 return *a + b
}

D.
type Integer int
func (a *Integer) Add(b *Integer) Integer {
 return *a + *b
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

AC If it’s func (a Integer), the compiler will automatically add func (a *Integer) for you. The reverse is not true.

item.title: Go Daily Question 090
item.description:
What is the output of the following code? Why?

type People interface {
 Speak(string) string
}

type Student struct{}

func (stu *Student) Speak(think string) (talk string) {
 if think == "speak" {
 talk = "speak"
 } else {
 talk = "hi"
 }
 return
}

func main() {
 var peo People = Student{}
 think := "speak"
 fmt.Println(peo.Speak(think))
}

A. speak B. compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

B Compilation error: Student does not implement People (Speak method has pointer receiver). The value type Student does not implement the Speak() method of the interface; instead, the pointer type *Student implements this method.

item.title: Go Daily Question 030
item.description:
Will the following code compile? Why?

package main

import (
 "fmt"
)

type People interface {
 Speak(string) string
}

type Student struct{}

func (stu *Student) Speak(think string) (talk string) {
 if think == "love" {
 talk = "You are a good boy"
 } else {
 talk = "hi"
 }
 return
}

func main() {
 var peo People = Student{}
 think := "love"
 fmt.Println(peo.Speak(think))
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

It will not compile because *Student implements the interface, not Student.
